title: The eighth: Mina
hook: pilgrims go to Mina, a city of tents

segments.voice: Yesterday, sa'y between Safa and Marwa, and your line: in her footsteps. What one thing did you do about a worry? Day one thousand one hundred thirty.

On the eighth day, where did the Prophet pray the noon prayer? Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay wanted a straight answer, so he asked Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: tell me something you remember. Anas answered: at Mina. The exchange is in Sahih al-Bukhari, and it's how the days of Hajj itself begin. Not at the Ka'ba. Outside the city, in a valley of tents. Today, the eighth.
screen: `WHERE DID HE PRAY AT NOON?` → `AT MINA.` → `A VALLEY OF TENTS.`

segments.voice: First, the date. The pilgrimage so far, the circling and the walking, can be done at other times of year too. Hajj proper has its own days in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, and in Jabir's account they begin on the eighth, the day of tarwiyah. Pilgrims who have come out of ihram enter it again, and the crowd moves out of Mecca to Mina. Second, what the Prophet did there. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says that on that day they set out for Mina, and the Prophet prayed there the noon, afternoon, sunset, evening and dawn prayers. Then he waited a little until the sun had risen, and went on. That's the whole of the eighth: travel, five prayers, one night, and waiting. No great ritual. A pause before Arafah. Third, the place now. Mina today is a valley filled with row after row of tents, white and fireproof, set up for the days of Hajj and almost empty the rest of the year. People from far and wide sleep side by side on thin mattresses, share food, queue for the washrooms, and pray together on carpets laid over the ground. The surgeon in white cloth from a week ago is now sharing a tent with strangers. Fourth, the end of Anas's answer. After the places and the prayers, he closed with a line: do as your leaders do. Pilgrims follow the group, move when it moves, rest when it rests. The Qur'an, in surah two, speaks of the days spent here later in the Hajj; in Pickthall's words: "Remember Allah through the appointed days." A city of tents is a place for exactly that: not much to do, and plenty of time to remember.
screen: `THE FIRST DAY OF HAJJ PROPER.` · `FIVE PRAYERS AND ONE NIGHT.` · `STRANGERS SIDE BY SIDE.` · `DO AS YOUR LEADERS DO.`

segments.voice: The practice: sit in a small space. Find somewhere snug, a corner of a room, the edge of a bed, a parked car, a closet floor if it's clean. Sit down there with nothing to do. Notice how close the walls are, and how little you need in it. If you pray, you can use the time for remembrance, a few words of praise you know, said slowly. If you don't, just stay with the breath and the smallness of the space. The bell holds the time.
The eighth. The eighth of Dhul-Hijjah, when pilgrims go out to Mina, pray, and spend the night in tents. Today's word.
Your line: a city of tents. Today, share a small space with someone without complaining about it: a bench, a line, a desk. Day one thousand one hundred thirty.

howItsDone: On the eighth of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims enter ihram for Hajj if they are not already in it and go to Mina, where they pray the day's prayers, shortening those of four units, and spend the night before moving on to Arafah.

notes: Bukhari 1653 (Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay asks Anas where the Prophet prayed zuhr on the day of tarwiyah: 'at Mina'; then 'do as your leaders do', which in the report concerns where to pray asr on the day of departure): confirm number, and that the summary of 'do as your leaders do' is fair.
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir: on the day of tarwiyah they went to Mina; the Prophet prayed zuhr, asr, maghrib, isha and fajr there, waited until sunrise): confirm.
Pickthall 2:203 quoted from memory: confirm. The verse is generally read as the days of tashriq at Mina after the day of sacrifice; the script says 'later in the Hajj'.
Description of modern Mina (white fireproof tents, nearly empty outside Hajj, people from far and wide): general color; confirm.
'Hajj proper has its own days ... the eighth is the first of them': standard description; confirm phrasing.
